title: UCP Requirements Catalog
description: The normative obligations stated in one page of a UCP specification, in machine-readable form. Produced by org-tools/requirements-extractor/scripts/extract_requirements.py in the Universal-Commerce-Protocol/.github repository, which writes one such file per specification page. Records carry no release of their own: the release is spec_version in this header, so cutting a release changes one line per file rather than every record. Once published, this file does not change; a change to the format ships as a new file whose name carries the new version.

schema_version.description: Semantic version of the catalog format, which names the schema file the catalog conforms to.

extractor_version.description: Version of the tool that produced the catalog.

spec_version.description: UCP release the specification tree represents, such as 'draft' or a dated release. This is the only place a catalog names its release: combined with a record's source.page and source.anchor, it gives the published link.

generated_at.description: UTC timestamp of the run. This is the only field that differs between two runs over identical input, so consumers comparing catalogs for drift must exclude it; --check does.

commit_sha.description: Commit the catalog was generated from, or null outside a git checkout.

source_file.description: Repository-relative path of the specification page this catalog describes, POSIX separators. Every record's source.file equals it.

requirements.description: The page's requirements, in source order. A page with none has no catalog file.

diagnostics.description: Counts per diagnostic bucket for this page. Every clause citing an RFC 2119 keyword either reaches the catalog or appears in one of these, so the totals reconcile.

id.description: Readable identifier for conformance tests to bind to. Read together with text_digest, it distinguishes a requirement that was reworded from one that was removed.

text_digest.description: First ten hex characters of the SHA-256 of the normalized compound_parent and the normalized clause, joined by U+001F. It depends on the wording alone, not on capability, file, line or heading, so it survives a page being relabelled or reorganized, and it can be recomputed from this record.

scope.description: Whether the requirement belongs to particular capabilities or to the protocol as a whole.

capabilities.description: Reverse-DNS identifiers of the capabilities the requirement belongs to: at least one when scope is 'capability', none when scope is 'protocol'.

target_actor.description: Uppercase party bound by the requirement, following the specification's own vocabulary (BUSINESS, not MERCHANT). Null when no actor could be attributed; guessing was measured and rejected as worse than admitting ignorance.

actor_confidence.description: Confidence of the strategy that resolved target_actor. 0 when unresolved.

clause.description: The obligation as written, Markdown emphasis intact.

normalized.description: Canonical form of the clause, used as digest input.

condition.description: Leading conditional the obligation is scoped by, verbatim, or null.

referenced_fields.description: Schema field names the clause names, deduplicated and sorted.

compound_parent.description: List stem or matrix context the clause inherits meaning from. A matrix cell reading only 'must' means nothing without it.

document_order.description: Position of the source block within its document.

start_line.description: 1-based first line of the enclosing block.

end_line.description: 1-based last line of the enclosing block, inclusive.

block_type.description: Markdown construct the clause was found in.

page.description: Site-relative path of the published page, without the release segment, such as 'specification/shopping/checkout/rest/'. The published link is the site root, the catalog's spec_version, this page and the anchor: https://ucp.dev/<spec_version>/<page>#<anchor>.

anchor.description: Fragment of the deepest heading above the clause, as the site renders it: the heading's explicit attr_list id when it has one, otherwise the renderer's own slugify of the heading. Null when the clause precedes every heading.
